subject: Urgent: persistent WebSocket timeouts during high-concurrency ramp demo
messages:
From: Priyanka Rao <pri@cliqa.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt Lee <ops@cliqa.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Demo failed: websocket timeouts & stalled chunks during our ramp

Hi Alex / Vanessa —

We had a scheduled ramp demo this morning (load test to ~250 concurrent live sessions) and ran into repeated WebSocket timeouts and long pauses where the model produced no chunks for 5–20s before resuming. The behavior broke our client-side progress indicators and caused the session to reconnect repeatedly.

Reproduction notes:
- Start 200–260 concurrent sessions using the streaming endpoint (wss://api.redwood/runtime/v1/stream)
- After ~6–10 minutes chunked transfer begins to stall for a subset of sessions
- Affected sessions show repeated WebSocket CLOSEs with 1006/timeout and server-side 504s in logs

Attached is a zip with a client trace, server headers we captured, and a small video of the UI flicker. This is blocking our pilot launch next week. Can you please confirm receipt and estimated time to remediate? We need either a short-term mitigation (disable streaming / route to non-stream API) or a timeline for a fix.

Thanks — Pri
Priyanka Rao
Senior Product Manager, Cliqa
pri@cliqa.com

We're pulling our on-call infra and runtime engineers now — Alex, I’m going to loop you in to prioritize. I’ll confirm the action we take in the next 15 minutes.

From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Priyanka Rao <pri@cliqa.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo failed: websocket timeouts & stalled chunks during our ramp

Thanks for the trace and the quick ping. Initial findings from infra+runtime:

What we're seeing
- Proxy (NGINX layer) upstream buffers and keepalive limits are being exhausted when concurrent streaming sessions exceed ~120 per proxy worker. When that happens, some TCP connections are held in a half-open state and chunked transfer stalls — client sees long silence then a timeout.
- The runtime continues to generate tokens but the proxy backpressure + buffer limits cause the socket to stop flushing at the TCP layer. In some cases the client reconnects and the session restarts, exacerbating the concurrency spike.
- Error rates in the logs line up with the timeline and the header sizes / SSE framing look normal — this points at proxy-level connection management under sustained concurrency.

Immediate mitigation (low-risk, can ship now)
1) Gate streaming for Cliqa: disable streaming for the tenant and switch them to the /responses (complete payload) endpoint. We can flip this per-tenant in the routing layer instantly.
2) Short-term proxy tweak: increase upstream_buffers and keepalive_timeout on affected proxy nodes and recycle workers (will need ~20–30 minutes to roll).
3) If customer allows, route traffic to the Dedicated warm spare (no code change) — immediate, but requires toggling routing policy.

Longer-term fixes
- Increase per-worker connection limits + introduce connection backpressure at accept-time to avoid buffer exhaustion.
- Improve runtime flush path so that when proxy buffers are full we shed backpressure earlier (avoids silent stalls).

Impact & ETA
- Option (1) gate streaming: ~5 minutes to flip and validate.
- Option (2) proxy config roll: ~30–90 minutes (staged upgrade to avoid collateral).
- Option (3) Dedicated route: ~10 minutes to flip routing, but consumes reserved capacity.

I recommend we first flip streaming off for Cliqa (option 1) to restore reliability for their demo, then apply the proxy buffer tweak to reduce chance of recurrence.

I opened INF-3321 for the investigation and assigned it to runtime infra. Attaching the proxy statistic dump.

— David
Head of Runtime Engineering
[Attachment: proxy-upstream-stats-20260811.txt]

Thank you for the quick reproduction steps and the trace. We have a recommended immediate path: disable streaming for your tenant and route you to the complete-response endpoint so your sessions return full responses instead of relying on chunked streaming. This will avoid silent chunk stalls while we deploy proxy configuration changes.

Can you confirm you are OK with us flipping that for the next 30–60 minutes while we stabilize? If yes, we will:
- Flip the tenant routing now
- Continue to push the proxy config change (staged) and keep you updated

If you prefer to stay on streaming, we can instead route you to a Dedicated warm spare and keep streaming live — please let us know preference and I’ll execute immediately.

Apologies again — we’ll get you back to green.

— Vanessa
